Text: "Paul Pogba, who plays for Manchester United and the French national team, retired from international football in response to French President Macron’s comments on Islamist terrorism."
Claim date: October 26, 2020
Claim origin: https://www.195sports.com/%D8%A8%D9%88%D9%84-%D8%A8%D9%88%D8%AC%D8%A8%D8%A7-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%AA%D8%B2%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%A8-%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%8B%D8%A7-%D8%A8%D8%B9%D8%AF-%D9%85%D8%A7-%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%AB/?utm_campaign=nabdapp.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=nabdapp.com&ocid=Nabd_App
before_justification: The fact-check refutes the claim by confirming that Paul Pogba did not retire from international football; instead, he [publicly denied the reports](https://onefootball.com/en/news/man-uniteds-paul-pogba-slams-fake-news-claims-that-hes-retiring-from-france-duty-31541245), calling them "unacceptable fake news." Evidence shows he [continued to be called up](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Paul_Pogba) for the French national team after October 2020, and there is no credible evidence linking any decision to retire to President Macron's comments on Islamist terrorism.
after_justification: The claim that Paul Pogba retired from international football due to French President Macron's comments on Islamist terrorism was reported by a non-credible blog. This assertion was not supported by major news organizations at the time and was explicitly denied by Paul Pogba himself, who labeled it "fake news". The retirement's purported reason, therefore, lacks credible evidence.

Paul Labile Pogba (born 15 March 1993) is a French professional footballer who plays for Serie A club Juventus and the France national team.
He operates primarily as a central midfielder, but can be deployed as a left winger, attacking midfielder, midfielder and deep-lying playmaker.
Born in Lagny-sur-Marne, Pogba joined the youth team of Ligue 1 side Le Havre in 2007, before a protracted transfer brought him to Manchester United two years later.
After beginning his senior career with Manchester United two years later, limited appearances persuaded him to depart to join Italian side Juventus on a free transfer in 2012, where he helped the club to four consecutive Serie A titles, as well as two Coppa Italia and two Supercoppa Italiana titles.
During his time in Italy, Pogba further established himself as one of the most promising young players in the world and received the Golden Boy award in 2013, followed by the Bravo Award in 2014.
In 2016, Pogba was named to the 2015 UEFA Team of the Year and the 2015 FIFA FIFPro World XI after helping Juventus to the 2015 UEFA Champions League Final, their first in 12 years.
Pogba's performances at Juventus led to him returning to Manchester United in 2016 for a then-orld record transfer fee of €105 million (£89.3 million).The fee was the highest paid by an English club until 2021.
In his first season back, he won the League Cup and the Europa League. In the 2018–19 season, he was named in the PFA Team of the Year.
Internationally, Pogba captained France to victory at the 2013 FIFA U-20 World Cup and took home the award for the Best Player for his performances during the tournament.
He made his debut for the senior team a year later and featured prominently at the 2014 FIFA World Cup, where he was awarded the Best Young Player Award for his performances.
He later represented his nation at UEFA Euro 2016 on home soil, where he finished as a runner-up, before winning the 2018 FIFA World Cup, scoring in the final.
